aadfe34d4fae9b78: KUALA LUMPUR: Lim Guan Eng (PH-Bagan) has proposed setting up a permanent Asean task force to tackle transboundary haze, in cooperation with Singapore, the Philippines and Indonesia.

Debating the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage in the Dewan Rakyat today, Lim said the task force should be supported by a year-round rescue team ready to respond immediately when forest fires occur.
He said if Indonesia continued to reject the task force on sovereignty grounds, Malaysia would have no choice but to pursue legal action to seek compensation.
"Malaysians cannot just remain silent in the face of this haze crisis without taking any action," he said.
Lim said the current crisis was driven by increasingly severe forest and land fires, with the affected area in Indonesia reaching 300,000ha this year, 70 per cent more than in 2023.

He also called on the government to provide special financial assistance to those affected by the haze, particularly gig economy workers and e-hailing drivers forced to stop work because of unhealthy air quality.

Meanwhile, Datuk Ali Biju (PN-Saratok) called on the government to explore international legal mechanisms to seek compensation from parties responsible for transboundary haze, including commercial plantation companies involved in open burning.
He said the recurring haze affected not only the health of millions across the Asean region but also tourism, businesses, transport and the hosting of international sporting events.
Ali expressed concern that the haze could disrupt the 2027 SEA Games in Sarawak, scheduled for September next year, as the phenomenon typically occurs during that period.
"This haze is a man-made disaster. It is predictable, deliberate, and continues to occur every year," he said.
He called on the government to lodge a formal complaint against Indonesia, strengthen laws on transboundary haze pollution and consider establishing a disaster fund to assist those affected.
Ali also called for stricter enforcement against parties involved in open burning.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting resumes on Monday.
677bd6efc363c3b1: KUALA LUMPUR: Majlis Pelancongan Kesihatan Malaysia (MHTC) dan Malayan Banking Bhd memeterai kerjasama berbilang tahun bagi meningkatkan akses kepada perkhidmatan kesihatan Malaysia untuk pelanggan Maybank di seluruh Asean.

Kerjasama ini akan menghubungkan pelanggan Maybank di rantau ini dengan rangkaian perkhidmatan kesihatan MHTC, menyediakan maklumat mengenai rawatan perubatan, kemudahan kesihatan, serta perkhidmatan sokongan yang terdapat di Malaysia. Inisiatif ini dijangka diperluaskan ke pasaran utama lain mulai 2027.

Kerjasama ini menyusuli penyertaan bersama MHTC dan Maybank di MH WellFest Cambodia 2026 pada awal Oktober, yang menyaksikan petugas kesihatan Malaysia menyampaikan ceramah kesihatan dan sesi konsultasi peribadi.
Indonesia, Filipina, dan Singapura dikenal pasti sebagai pasaran keutamaan untuk fasa inisiatif yang seterusnya.

Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif MHTC, Suriaghandi Suppiah, berkata usaha mendapatkan rawatan perubatan di luar negara bukan sekadar memilih hospital. Pesakit juga perlu memahami sistem perkhidmatan kesihatan yang tidak biasa, menguruskan kos, serta membuat persiapan untuk ahli keluarga yang menemani.
Beliau berkata walaupun Malaysia mempunyai 91 kemudahan kesihatan yang diiktiraf MHTC, memastikan pesakit dapat mencapai dan menggunakan perkhidmatan tersebut adalah sama penting.
"Kualiti sahaja tidak membawa pesakit ke sini. Akses yang membawa mereka ke sini," kata Suriaghandi pada majlis tandatangan di Menara Merdeka Maybank.

"Kami akan membina kerjasama ini berasaskan apa yang telah kami pelajari di Kemboja, memperkemaskannya bersama-sama, dan menilai perkara yang berkesan. Berpandukan kepada hasilnya, kami akan membawa pendekatan ini ke pasaran utama lain di serata Asean mulai 2027," katanya.
Pelaksanaan awal akan menyaksikan pelanggan Maybank Premier di Kemboja mendapat akses kepada maklumat perkhidmatan kesihatan dan kesejahteraan melalui rangkaian MHTC.
Di Indonesia, pelanggan akan mendapat akses kepada keistimewaan dan sokongan berkaitan perkhidmatan kesihatan.
MHTC juga akan membantu hospital swasta Malaysia menjangkau lebih ramai pesakit antarabangsa melalui pelanggan Maybank di Asean.

Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Kumpulan Perkhidmatan Kewangan Komuniti Maybank, Syed Ahmad Taufik Albar, berkata kerjasama ini mencerminkan usaha bank untuk menyokong keperluan pelanggan yang semakin melangkaui perbankan konvensional.

"Di serata Asean, pelanggan kami menjalani kehidupan yang semakin mudah bergerak, dengan keperluan dan keutamaan yang merentasi pasaran. Dengan rangkaian perbankan merentasi 10 negara Asean, Maybank berada pada kedudukan yang baik untuk memenuhi keperluan yang berkembang ini dalam cara yang melangkaui perbankan tradisional,” katanya dalam kenyataan bersama.
Kerjasama ini menyokong inisiatif Tahun Pelancongan Perubatan Malaysia 2026 dan usaha Kementerian Kesihatan memperkukuh kedudukan Malaysia sebagai destinasi pelancongan perubatan pilihan.
b431d2022934381f: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should reconsider its decision to scrap plans for an international airport on Pulau Tioman to ease access for more than 3,600 residents and support tourism, says an opposition MP.

Abdul Khalib Abdullah (PN-Rompin) said the island, a gazetted marine park, draws about 250,000 tourists annually, but its near-total reliance on sea transport makes movement, local logistics and economic activities difficult.
“Conserving Tioman is a shared trust. However, conservation and connectivity are not two opposing things.
"Cancelling the project does not solve the access problems for residents and operators on the island," he said while debating the 2027 budget in the Dewan Rakyat.

The Cabinet decided in August 2023 not to proceed with the proposed Tioman International Airport after an environmental impact assessment found that the project, which involved reclaiming 76% of the sea area, could significantly harm marine ecology.
The assessment identified 120 species of hard coral and 12 species of soft coral in the area.
On ferry travel, Khalib urged operators of the Teluk Gading-Pulau Tioman route to cancel the new fare hike, which he said burdened tourists and residents.
He said higher fares at a time of economic difficulty could hurt tourist arrivals and the income of businesses on the island.
"I also urge the government to intervene by reviewing the basis for the fare increase, in addition to ensuring that comfortable and quality services are provided," said Khalib.
ae462a0d2c28f1d3: JAKARTA: Indonesia has approved offers of assistance from neighbouring countries to help combat widespread forest and land fires, with technical discussions underway to determine the arrangements.

Indonesian Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir said President Prabowo Subianto had approved the proposed assistance, with the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) now holding technical-level discussions on its implementation.
"Offers of assistance form neighbouring countries have already been discussed and is now being processed.

"As we know, the president has also given his approval, and the matter is now under discussion at the technical level," he told reporters after a closed-door meeting with parliament's Commission I in Jakarta.
Arrmanatha did not identify the countries involved or specify the types of assistance being considered.

Malaysia had earlier offered to deploy a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 52 personnel to help Indonesia tackle the fires, with Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announcing on Sept 19 that Prabowo had approved the offer during their meeting in Hambalang, West Java, a day earlier.

Singapore has also expressed its readiness to assist Indonesia, with Minister for Sustainability and the Environment Grace Fu saying on Oct 10 that she had contacted her Indonesian counterpart, Jumhur Hidayat, to offer support in combating the fires.

Arrmanatha said the fires were receiving serious attention from Prabowo because of their significant impact on haze-affected areas, while challenging weather conditions continued to hamper firefighting efforts.
He said about 60,000 personnel had been deployed across six priority provinces, supported by helicopters and aircraft for water bombing and weather modification operations.

On regional cooperation, Arrmanatha said Indonesia had fulfilled its regular reporting obligations under the Asean Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control (ACC THPC) mechanism since August.

He said Indonesia had regularly shared data on the fire situation, mitigation measures and developments with the Asean Secretariat, which serves as the interim coordinating centre. The latest reports indicated progress, including a reduction in hotspot numbers.

Meanwhile, newly appointed BNPB chief Lieutenant General Kristomei Sianturi said he would first assess resources available to regional and central governments, alongside foreign assistance that could be expedited to strengthen firefighting operations.

"I will first take stock of our available assets, what we can already do at the regional and central government levels, and what assistance from abroad we can jointly expedite," he told reporters after his swearing-in ceremony at the State Palace on Thursday, according to a livestream by the Presidential Secretariat.

Kristomei, who replaced Lieutenant General Suharyanto as BNPB chief said combating the fires required collective action involving communities, regional administrations and the central government, rather than relying solely on the disaster management agency.
4dc1cfe494328fc0: WUHAN: Iga Swiatek hit a new milestone on Thursday as she stormed into a second consecutive Wuhan Open quarter-final with a 6-1, 6-4 win over American lucky loser Ashlyn Krueger.
The six-time Grand Slam champion recorded the 150th WTA 1000 victory of her career to continue her march towards a 13th title at this level.

Since the Tier I/WTA 1000 format's introduction in 1990, Swiatek is just the third player to claim 150 wins from her first 50 main-draw appearances in such events, after Martina Hingis (162) and Serena Williams (153).

"I just wanted to focus on adjusting and being brave and, at the end, I’m happy that I was," said the seventh-seeded Swiatek, who needs a title this week to strengthen her chances of qualifying for next month’s WTA Finals in Indian Wells.
"For sure I feel like I am playing better than at the beginning of the season, so I'm ready to push and I'm happy to be in the quarters for sure," she said.
The 25-year-old Pole, who awaits Ann Li or Janice Tjen in the quarter-finals, is one of just two top-10 seeds still standing in a draw that has witnessed a slew of high-profile exits.
A day after the shocking departures of the top two seeds, Aryna Sabalenka and Jessica Pegula, sixth-seeded Karolina Muchova and 10th-seeded Iva Jovic also bid Wuhan farewell.
Maja Chwalinska, a finalist at the French Open this year, enjoyed a 6-4, 6-1 triumph over American world number 11 Jovic to set up a quarter-final with Greece's Maria Sakkari.
Diana Shnaider’s 7-5, 6-3 victory against Muchova was the Russian’s fourth career triumph over a top-10 opponent.
The 22-year-old will next take on Jelena Ostapenko for a place in the final four.
British world number 170 Sonay Kartal sent another seed packing after knocking out ninth-seeded Belinda Bencic in the second round.
This time she delivered a crushing 6-2, 6-0 blow to last year’s Wuhan semi-finalist Jasmine Paolini, the number 15 seed.
World number six Elina Svitolina avoided the seed exodus as she eased into the quarter-finals by ending the inspired run of Chinese wild card Guo Hanyu 6-1, 6-4.
1039933cf20297a0: Bank of America recruited an additional 1,000 contractors to help patch all the vulnerabilities discovered by Anthropic’s Mythos model, the CEO said on Wednesday. Brian Moynihan, chairman and CEO at BoA, said during the company’s Q3 earnings call that it spent “a couple of hundred million plus” in remediation costs related to Mythos, and the anti-money laundering (AML) orders issued this week. These costs are expected to decline over time, though, with the contractors in place to help ease the initial burden of patching a large number of flaws, an issue that shouldn’t be so pronounced in the longer term. He went on to tell CNBC that the bank brought in outside help after concerns grew over how it would quickly tackle all the work associated with Mythos’ discoveries. The same concerns were shared globally, in part due to how Anthropic marketed Mythos as an all-powerful model that threatened the status quo of cybersecurity. While it ultimately turned out to be highly effective and capable of identifying complex vulnerabilities quicker than humans, leading to the massive influx of patches, some early adopters say it was no smarter than elite researchers. Mozilla CTO Bobby Holley said in April: "So far we've found no category or complexity of vulnerability that humans can find that this model can't," after Mythos found 271 flaws in Firefox 150. "We also haven't seen any bugs that couldn't have been found by an elite human researcher." The 1,000 contractors brought in by the bank in its Q2 added to its existing 3,000 technical staff. The contractors remain at the bank for now, although their assistance won’t be needed in the longer term. Moynihan told financial analysts on the bank’s earnings call that BoA has made its tech engineering workforce around 10 percent more efficient, and that each of the circa 130 AI-related projects it has running is expected to achieve a 2x or 3x return on investment over time. In 2026 alone, the CEO expects AI projects to deliver between $250 million and $300 million in benefits – a sum he expects to shoot up to $700 million by the end of 2027. He didn't detail how. The bank has also reduced around 3,000 roles, including a 5 percent decrease in the number of managers on the payroll, although it didn't specify how much of a role AI played. Moynihan didn’t break down how much of the “couple of hundred million plus” in remediation costs were devoted to AI or Mythos, compared to costs associated with cleaning up its AML issues, both of which the CEO lumped together. BoA’s share price slid more than 8 percent on Wednesday morning after it reported a 17 percent drop in profits owing to the $1.21 billion settlement it agreed to with the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN). The FinCEN order relates to BoA’s failure to police national security risks, including Chinese money laundering, and a failure to report over $5 billion in suspicious activity. FinCEN’s order was issued concurrently with a $750 million penalty from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, related to Bank Secrecy Act and AML compliance deficiencies. BoA also agreed an $11.6 million settlement with the Office of Foreign Assets Control for sanctions violations, including those related to Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism. ®
eddfad7e773c5cae: NEW YORK: Actor Bryan Cranston is in "deep despair" following the death of his onscreen son, RJ Mitte, who died by suicide on Monday at the age of 34.
Mitte was best known for playing Walter White Jr. (Walt Jr.) across all five seasons of Breaking Bad.
Diagnosed with mild cerebral palsy when he was three years old, Mitte shared the same condition as his television character.
In 2013, he received the SAG-AFTRA Harold Russell Award—given in honour of Russell, the first actor with a disability to win an Oscar—for his landmark portrayal.

Paying tribute on Instagram, Cranston shared his heartbreak over the loss of his former co-star: "RJ Mitte, my sweet son on Breaking Bad, has died. I met him when he was only 14 years old, when he was cast as Walter White Jr., a part he played with such joy and enthusiasm," Cranston wrote.
"Born with Cerebral Palsy, he never – ever – allowed that challenge to be an excuse for anything," he continued. "He met the demanding shooting schedule head-on with great determination."

Cranston also celebrated Mitte's activism, calling him a "vocal advocate for performers with disabilities," and noted that he "was the head of a philanthropic organisation with a focus on helping the disabled community."
"It is especially devastating to hear that he took his own life," Cranston wrote. "Why?"
The actor went on to reveal that they had recently been texting and trying to arrange a lunch together, though it ultimately never happened.

"I don't know if that lunch would have changed his future," Cranston wrote. "But I do know that I loved him, and thoroughly enjoyed being with him throughout the years on the series, and after the spotlight on Breaking Bad dimmed." Cranston added: "I'll miss you, son."
The Emmy winner also encouraged "anyone who is contemplating suicide to please call for the support you need."
Fellow Breaking Bad cast members Dean Norris (DEA agent Hank Schrader) and Aaron Paul (Jesse Pinkman) also paid heartfelt tributes to their late co-star.

Norris called the news "heartbreaking" in a social media statement: "Though RJ didn't play my TV son, I always looked out for him as a young kid on set," Norris wrote. "He was a sweetheart of a young man and will be greatly missed. This is so heartbreaking, I can't believe it. Thinking of him and his family."
Paul admitted he was "at a loss" for words in a statement shared with The Hollywood Reporter: "RJ, I love you, my friend. You will be missed," Paul said.
"And to whoever happens to be reading this, please know you are loved, and you are not alone. Always remember that."
If you are feeling distressed or have any emotional problems, seek help from a medical professional or reach out to Befrienders at 03-7627 2929.
e998a311c7d3e958: PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court has refused a tobacco company’s bid to challenge a ruling ordering it to pay RM302,400 to its former national security manager for unfair dismissal over an alleged incident of inappropriate touching at a private club.

A three-member Federal Court bench, chaired by Justice Nordin Hassan, unanimously rejected Tobacco Importers and Manufacturers Sdn Bhd’s application for leave to appeal, ruling that its proposed questions of law did not meet the threshold under Section 96 of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964.
Justices Ahmad Terrirudin Salleh and Azimah Omar sat on the panel, which also ordered the company to pay RM50,000 in costs to the former employee.
In May, the Court of Appeal upheld the Industrial Court’s finding that the manager had been dismissed without just cause or excuse.

In a judgment delivered by Justice Azhahari Kamal Ramli, the appellate court said the company had dropped the word “sexual” and relied instead on “harassment” when framing the charge against the manager during the domestic inquiry and proceedings before the Industrial Court.

Azhahari said the omission had serious repercussions on the burden of proof the company had to discharge. He also ruled that the company’s Standard of Business Conduct should not be extended outside the workplace.
Justices Ahmad Kamal Shahid and Ahmad Shahrir Salleh were the other members of the Court of Appeal bench.
The case arose from an incident after the company’s annual dinner at a hotel in Kuala Lumpur on Nov 23, 2019.
The manager and a female employee, along with other guests, later adjourned to Wicked Club, a private entertainment outlet at the same hotel.
The woman subsequently complained that the manager had touched her without her consent between 1am and 2am on Nov 24. The manager had denied the allegation.

The woman claimed he had held her around the left side of her lower waist from behind in what was described as a semi-hug. She immediately told him, “Do not touch me”, pushed his hand away and walked off.
The Industrial Court found that the company could not frame the dismissal on sexual harassment during disciplinary proceedings and subsequently argued that the conduct amounted merely to harassment.
It also found that the company's code did not cover employee misconduct outside the workplace.
In 2022, the Industrial Court ordered RM302,400 in compensation instead of reinstatement and back wages. The High Court later dismissed the company's judicial review application to quash the award.
Steven Thiru, Janice Annie Leo and Adrienne Sena appeared for the company, while VK Raj and SP Devi represented the former manager in today's proceedings.
86c70288ab0d38ad: KUALA LUMPUR: Foreigners make up a small proportion of patients at Health Ministry facilities, the ministry said today.
In a statement, the ministry said its healthcare services continue to be fully utilised by Malaysians.
It said it regularly monitored trends in healthcare facility usage among non-citizens to plan capacity and safeguard public health.
The ministry said its patient information and registration systems strictly categorised admissions by citizenship status, namely citizens and non-citizens.
"This classification is important to ensure accurate implementation of medical fee collection procedures at registration counters.
"Medical registration records are not categorised according to sub-ethnic groups," it said.
The clarification follows claims circulating on social media that increasing numbers of foreigners were seeking treatment at government hospitals and clinics.
The ministry said its healthcare facilities were established and prioritised to meet the welfare and medical needs of Malaysians.
However, in line with basic medical ethics, emergency treatment to save lives would be provided to any patient based on urgent clinical needs.

"To ensure the sustainability of the public healthcare system and compliance with financial governance, non-Malaysian patients, including holders of United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cards, are charged full fees and higher deposits under the Fees (Medical) (Cost of Services) Order 2014.

"The ministry also enforces revenue collection through a 'collect before discharge' approach, which involves optimising the collection of deposits and treatment charges while patients are still warded.
"For outstanding bills, follow-up action is taken in stages in accordance with financial procedures, including the issuance of reminder letters and legal notices," it said.

The ministry added that it also worked with relevant agencies and non-governmental organisations to facilitate financial assistance for patients in genuine need without placing an additional burden on public funds.
489a75b22352fda7: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are tracking down a woman who kicked an auxiliary policeman in the groin after he confronted her for driving against traffic flow near a shopping complex in Damansara yesterday.
Police have identified the suspect and believed that she could be on the run.
Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said the incident occurred at 8.38am while the 30-year-old auxiliary policeman was on duty.
He said the policeman noticed a Hyundai Inokom parked facing the wrong direction, with its driver honking at other vehicles without reason.
The officer approached the woman and advised her to move the vehicle.
"However, the suspect showed an obscene gesture," Hoo said when contacted.
He said the woman then got out of the vehicle and attempted to attack the policeman before kicking him in the groin.
The policeman sought help from other personnel as he struggled with the woman and tried to restrain her, but she managed to flee.
"Efforts to track down the suspect are ongoing," Hoo said.
The case is being investigated under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act for insulting behaviour.
96a8f9533f16849d: PETALING JAYA: Seorang Ahli Parlimen menggesa kerajaan mempercepat pelaksanaan Dasar Gaji Progresif (DGP) secara mandatori bagi sektor swasta, beserta insentif subsidi gaji bagi membantu majikan menampung kos kenaikan upah pekerja.
Khairil Nizam Khirudin (PN-Jerantut) berkata, langkah itu perlu bagi menangani penyusutan kuasa beli rakyat akibat kenaikan harga barangan makanan asas yang mendahului pertumbuhan pendapatan benar.
"Penyusutan kuasa beli akibat kadar inflasi barangan makanan asas yang meningkat antara 3.0% hingga 4.5%, jauh mendahului pertumbuhan pendapatan benar.
"Penanda aras gaji median sektor swasta sebanyak RM2,600 sebulan tidak lagi mencukupi untuk menampung kos sara hidup semasa," katanya ketika membahaskan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat.

Dalam pada itu, Khairil berkata, generasi 'sandwich' turut berdepan tekanan kewangan apabila terpaksa menanggung kos perubatan ibu bapa yang semakin berusia, selain perbelanjaan persekolahan anak-anak.

Keadaan itu, katanya, lebih membimbangkan apabila lebih 50% ahli Kumpulan Wang Simpanan Pekerja (KWSP) berusia bawah 55 tahun dilaporkan mempunyai simpanan kurang daripada RM10,000, sedangkan Malaysia dijangka menjadi negara tua menjelang 2040.
Sehubungan itu, beliau mengemukakan empat cadangan kepada Kementerian Kewangan bagi membantu golongan berkenaan, termasuk mengiktiraf generasi 'sandwich' sebagai kumpulan sasaran dasar kerajaan.
Beliau turut mencadangkan pelepasan cukai khas kepada mereka yang membeli insurans perubatan untuk ibu bapa.
"Selain itu, kerajaan boleh memperkenalkan cuti penjagaan berbayar atau perlindungan pendapatan bagi pekerja yang menjaga ibu bapa atau tanggungan yang sakit dan uzur.
"Kerajaan juga perlu menyelaraskan akses kepada bantuan sedia ada supaya golongan berkenaan lebih mudah mendapatkan sokongan kewangan yang diperlukan," katanya.
125a640a53580ba4: BEIRUT: A Hezbollah MP acknowledged Thursday that a 500kg shipment of explosives seized last week by Lebanese authorities belonged to the group, a rare admission by the Iran-backed militants.
"The vehicle and its cargo belong to the resistance" against Israel, lawmaker Hassan Fadlallah said.
He said Hezbollah also called for the immediate release of those arrested over the seizure.
Fadlallah demanded the return of the shipment, seized on a road linking eastern Lebanon to Beirut, saying it constituted "capabilities" used by Hezbollah against Israel.
Lebanese prime minister Nawaf Salam has said the state will no longer tolerate any possession of "illegal weapons".
A judicial source told AFP the explosives were seized from a vehicle that was carrying 250kg of TNT and 250kg of the explosive C-4.
Salam has said authorities will "identify all individuals involved in this criminal operation and those who ordered it".
He said Lebanese people would be concerned by the seizure, especially since C-4 has previously been used in political assassinations in Lebanon.
At the beginning of this decade Hezbollah was accused of carrying out several political killings.
The group, which once dominated political life in Lebanon, has been weakened by two wars it waged against Israel since 2023.
Since a ceasefire in June, Hezbollah has not claimed any further attacks against Israel.
The Lebanese army has seized two other explosives shipments since the beginning of the month in the east of the country, near the border with Syria.
Since the fall of former Syrian president Bashar al-Assad at the end of 2024, the two countries have been working to eradicate smuggling across their porous border.
9889d375a4853d7f: PETALING JAYA: The Court of Appeal today upheld the dismissal of a suit by 21 contractors against the attorney-general, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner and three others over alleged wrongful detention and malicious prosecution.
Bernama reported that a three-member bench comprising Justices Choo Kah Sing, Evrol Mariette Peters and Nadzarin Wok Nordin dismissed the appeal as lacking merit.

Delivering the court’s decision, Choo said the appellants' complaint – that they had been forcibly detained from Nov 16 to 17, 2014, and held at a place not gazetted for detention under the law – was misplaced.

“With regard to the complaint of malicious prosecution, this court finds that the mere fact that the appellants were found not liable at the close of the prosecution’s case in the sessions court does not equate to malicious prosecution.
“Weak evidence and poor prosecution are not malicious prosecution,” he said.

Choo also said the appellants were charged based on an independent report by the public works department, adding that while the prosecution could have misapprehended the facts or misjudged the strength of the evidence, it could not be concluded that there was no probable or reasonable cause to prosecute the appellants.
He also said the High Court was correct to find the appellants' claim for false imprisonment was time-barred.
The appellants were arrested by MACC over investigations relating to the alleged misappropriation of funds for a project to repair fishermen's housing in 2014.
They were subsequently charged in the Kuala Terengganu sessions court and released on bail on Nov 17, 2014.
On July 31, 2017, the sessions court discharged and acquitted them at the end of the prosecution’s case. The prosecution filed an appeal but subsequently withdrew it on Feb 22, 2019.
Nearly seven years after their arrest, the appellants filed a civil suit against five defendants, including the attorney-general, the MACC chief commissioner, a MACC officer, MACC and the government.
They sought, among others, general damages and aggravated damages of RM1 million each and RM10 million in exemplary damages for all the appellants.
On May 8 this year, the Kuala Terengganu High Court dismissed the appellants' suit.

Rafaei Adnan and Alif Danial Ahmad Shahrulnizam represented the appellants in the Court of Appeal today, while senior federal counsel Liew Horng Bin and federal counsel Ahmad Faiz Abd Raoff represented the MACC and the government.
effaebc5e166d3b9: TSMC is dispatching personnel to check out US datacenter construction and power availability as it plans billions of dollars in additional chipmaking capacity. The Taiwanese chipmaking giant warned of pressure on consumer markets during its third-quarter earnings call, while maintaining that AI demand - at least for now - continues to outstrip supply. "Looking ahead, we continue to observe consumer and price-sensitive end market segments are being challenged due to the impact of rising component prices and macroeconomic uncertainties. As such, we are being prudent in our business planning going into 2027," said chairman and CEO C.C. Wei. Wei said AI demand remained strong, with CPUs for agentic workloads and networking chips adding to the need for silicon. "Therefore, semiconductors will remain essential in the AI mega trend. The value of semiconductors in the global supply chain is set to continue to increase in our view," he stated. TSMC expects capital expenditure of $60 billion to $64 billion this year. Spending across 2026-2028 is expected to exceed the total for 2023-2025 as it expands capacity for customers. Those plans depend on more than customers ordering chips: the datacenters housing them also need power, networking, memory, and other infrastructure. TSMC is checking how those pieces are coming together before committing to expanding capacity further. TSMC is planning roughly 20 leading-edge manufacturing and advanced-packaging facilities in Taiwan and overseas over the next several years, and Wei said the contract manufacturer is also focusing on capacity optimization across production nodes to generate more wafer output. One analyst on the earnings call asked whether power shortages, datacenter construction delays, advanced-packaging constraints, or limited supplies of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) could hold back projected growth. Wei said TSMC factors these constraints into its capacity planning. "We put every possibility we can, talking about the cloud service providers, capex, datacenter build-out, financial, power supply, and also other component supply, all into our consideration. "We make our own judgment, and then based on our assessment of the demand, we still think the demand is higher than the supply, and we are working very hard to narrow the gap." However, he declined to directly answer a question about whether he expected tightness in the wafer supply to be greater next year than this year, saying "the demand is extremely robust and getting higher and higher." Wei said preparations for A14, TSMC's next-generation process marketed as 1.4 nm, were underway. He expects it to become a bigger business than the current 2 nm generation. Risk production – an initial manufacturing phase ahead of commercial ramp-up – is scheduled for 2027, followed by volume production in 2028. For the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, TSMC reported revenue of $46.72 billion, an increase of 41.2 percent on the same period a year ago. Looking to the fourth quarter, the company expects another jump in revenue, to between $52.3 billion and $54.3 billion. At the midpoint, that would represent roughly 58 percent year-on-year growth. ®
73eb85ab5e34b46c: PUTRAJAYA: Mahkamah Rayuan hari ini mengekalkan keputusan Mahkamah Tinggi menolak saman 21 kontraktor terhadap peguam negara, ketua pesuruhjaya Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) dan tiga lagi berhubung dakwaan penahanan salah serta pendakwaan berniat jahat.
Panel tiga hakim terdiri daripada Choo Kah Sing, Evrol Mariette Peters dan Nadzarin Wok Nordin membuat keputusan itu selepas menolak rayuan tersebut atas alasan ia tidak mempunyai merit.

Semasa menyampaikan keputusan mahkamah, Choo berkata, aduan perayu bahawa mereka telah dipenjarakan secara paksa dari 16 Nov hingga 17 Nov 2014 dan tidak ditahan di tempat yang diwartakan bagi tujuan penahanan mengikut lunas undang-undang adalah tidak berasas.

“Berhubung isu pendakwaan berniat jahat, mahkamah ini mendapati hakikat bahawa perayu didapati tidak dipertanggungjawabkan pada akhir kes pendakwaan di Mahkamah Sesyen tidak boleh disamakan dengan pendakwaan berniat jahat.

Choo juga berkata, Mahkamah Tinggi membuat keputusan yang tepat dengan memutuskan bahawa tindakan undang-undang yang difailkan oleh para perayu berhubung dakwaan pemenjaraan salah telah luput tempoh masa.

Para perayu, terdiri daripada Razali Dollah; Zakaria Jusoh; Rahim Mohamad; Shariman Azam Shafie; Zamri Abdul Mana; Che Forzi Che Abd Aziz; Abdul Rahim Awang; Mohamad Nizam Wahit; Enche Baharuddin Enche Endut; Salim Berahim; Ahmad Atma Ali@Yusof; Abdullah Embong; Othman Omar; Mohd Ramadhan Baharudin; Mohd Amir Ismadi Md Ghani; Mohd Zaid Ahmad@Mat; Mohamad Sari Ngah; Abdul Rashid Muda; Yusof Omar; Fakru Prazi Nordin; dan Shahairi Abd Wahab, telah ditahan oleh SPRM bagi membantu siasatan kes penyelewengan projek membaik pulih rumah nelayan pada 2014.

Hampir tujuh tahun selepas ditahan, para perayu memfailkan saman dan menamakan peguam negara, ketua pesuruhjaya SPRM, SPRM, kerajaan Malaysia serta seorang pegawai agensi antirasuah itu.
Antara lain, mereka menuntut ganti rugi am dan ganti rugi teruk berjumlah RM1 juta bagi setiap orang serta ganti rugi teladan berjumlah RM10 juta bagi kesemua perayu.
Pada 8 Mei lepas, Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Terengganu menolak saman kesemua perayu.

Pada prosiding hari ini, Mohammad Rafaei Adnan dan Alif Danial Ahmad Shahrulnizam mewakili kesemua perayu manakala Peguam Kanan Persekutuan Liew Horng Bin serta Peguam Persekutuan Ahmad Faiz Abd Raoff hadir bagi pihak SPRM dan kerajaan.
80c01b0aa70e1a76: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia’s gross domestic product (GDP) is expected to grow by 5.2% in 2026 and 4.7% in 2027, amid regional economic uncertainty, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

In its October 2026 Regional Economic Outlook for Asia and the Pacific, themed “Resilient Amid Uncertainty: Can It Be Sustained?”, the IMF highlighted technology-related exports and strong investment in data centres as key contributors to growth across the region.

“Malaysia and Singapore have increased exports as assemblers and packagers of technology products, while strong investment in data centres in China, India, Japan, Indonesia and Malaysia has also contributed to growth,” it said in its report today.
The investment in data centres has generated broader demand for intermediate goods from regional suppliers, including Thailand and Vietnam.
In Malaysia, operational data centre capacity stood at more than 1,000 megawatts (MW), with a further 1,500MW under construction, according to the report.
“As for the composition of services exports, modern services in Malaysia accounted for about 30% of total services exports in 2023, while traditional services made up the remainder.
“Across Asean, services exports embodied in goods exports accounted for 17%, while services exports delivered through a commercial presence accounted for 30%,” the report said.

However, the IMF noted that many services exports in the region remain oriented towards global markets rather than regional markets, particularly modern services, of which only 14%, on average, are exported to countries within the Asia-Pacific region.
On inflation, the report said the pass-through of higher energy prices to both headline and core inflation had remained relatively contained in most advanced and emerging market economies.
“This was partly due to reliance on inventories and the widespread use of price-smoothing measures, including in Malaysia, Korea and Thailand,” it added.

Containing the pass-through of higher energy prices has been the main policy objective, with more than 80% of economies adopting measures to limit the impact on domestic prices, using an average of two to four instruments.
These measures included fuel or utility price freezes and subsidies in Malaysia, alongside fuel tax and duty reductions in Cambodia and Laos, and subsidy-backed fuel price caps in Japan and Thailand.
Targeted support has also complemented broader measures to channel relief to exposed sectors and households. These included credit guarantees or liquidity facilities in Malaysia, India and Singapore.
Demand-side measures, such as work-from-home arrangements, shorter public sector hours and travel restrictions, have also been implemented in Malaysia and several other economies in the region.

On domestic demand, the IMF pointed out that Malaysia's per capita consumption had grown faster than income, with a higher differential than the average among emerging market and developing economies, aided by a notable increase in household borrowing from banks.

For economies where consumption growth was relatively robust, including Malaysia and Thailand, the IMF said policies should focus on strengthening the resilience of consumption, particularly among vulnerable and highly indebted households.
d9be23f4c8dc3b47: WASHINGTON, Oct 15 — One message told him to “go to hell.” Others said he deserved to be imprisoned. Death threats poured in.
Asians who share a name with one of the men accused of raping a US university student have faced a torrent of online abuse.

The alleged 2024 gang rape of a Cornell University student, detailed in a recent lawsuit, has sparked an outpouring of outrage against the seven accused perpetrators. The case has sent internet sleuths scouring digital footprints for clues to track them down.
One of the accused is a Korean man identified by US media as Winston Lee.
The problem is that the world is full of people named Winston Lee.

The rage misdirected at people who share that name, some of whom live outside the US and look nothing like the accused, lays bare the perils of a chaotic internet, where people distrustful of public institutions become digital detectives.

One of those wrongly identified was a Chinese American whose LinkedIn profile identifies him as a New York-based finance professional who graduated from Cornell University in 2020 — four years before the alleged rape.
“You can’t hide. Your future is over,” said one message he received via LinkedIn.
“You’ll get exactly what you deserve...which is prison!! You’ll be gang raped there.”
Another said that a “black magic” spell had been cast upon him.
In a video on TikTok — where his bio reads “Not part of Cornell7” — he said he had hired a lawyer to press charges against a woman who posted his phone number and his parents’ address online.
‘Mob’
After a deluge of hateful messages, another man misidentified as Winston Lee posted a personal appeal to TikTok detectives.
“I am Indonesian and not the Winston Lee named in the recent Cornell University case,” he said.
“Please verify the identity of the person you are looking for before contacting, tagging, or making accusations against someone.”
After a similar flood of messages, a Chinese-American student named Winston Lee at the University of Pennsylvania added a disclaimer to his LinkedIn profile: “I do not go to Cornell.”
Those appeals did not appear to slow what Reddit discussion boards described as an “online hunt” for the seven accused, drawing many users down internet rabbit holes.
With few verified details about the man actually accused, internet users continued searching aggressively for his whereabouts.
One Reddit post claimed Winston Lee was now serving in the South Korean army. Another user on X said she had received tips suggesting Lee had been spotted on Cornell University’s campus.
People with names like the other six accused also complained about rage spamming and threats.
“These social justice warriors are literally messaging and harassing the wrong” people, said podcast host Brad Polumbo.
“These things should be litigated through the criminal process or through some sort of fair process, not through a social media mob or witch hunt.”
‘Hounded’
A group of former Cornell students, who belonged to the same Chi Phi fraternity as the seven accused but graduated before the alleged incident, also complained of online smear campaigns.

“They are being wrongfully accused on social media of having involvement, are consequently receiving death threats and related hate mail,” their attorney Adam Ford wrote in a letter to the university that was obtained by AFP.
“Most of them have had their employers and higher education institutions take adverse actions against them, including being placed on leave.”
Digital sleuths have for years misidentified accused perpetrators of high-profile shootings and other crimes, exposing them to abuse.

Such misidentification can further roil an already chaotic information ecosystem and hinder the actual investigation by generating false leads, warned Mike Rothschild, a researcher who studies conspiracy theories.
“The wrongfully accused are often hounded,” Rothschild told AFP.
“They sometimes have to go into hiding, or get death threats, or are even violently attacked themselves. And there is no penalty for being wrong on the part of those accusing them.” — AFP
5ad004d927d90629: WASHINGTON, Oct 15 — A typhoon in the Philippines and flooding in Brazil. Twice in less than a year, British energy giant Shell has been the target of a new type of lawsuit seeking to make polluters pay part of the cost of specific extreme weather events.
“We chose Shell because it’s an emblematic company. It meets all the criteria,” Thales Miola, a lawyer for the Brazilian NGO Instituto Preservar, told AFP.
On tomorrow, the organisation and federal prosecutors jointly filed a lawsuit against Shell’s subsidiary in South America’s largest country.

They are seeking the equivalent of US$108 million (RM441 million) in compensation for catastrophic flooding in southern Brazil in 2024. The disaster killed nearly 200 people, displaced half a million and caused widespread destruction.
Until now, the only lawsuits filed over the disaster had targeted public authorities.

Shell is not Brazil’s biggest oil company — that distinction belongs to state-owned Petrobras — but it has operated there for decades, and its contribution to global warming is well-documented and “a huge amount for a single company,” Miola said.
According to estimates by the think tank Carbon Majors cited in the lawsuit, Shell holds responsibility for 2.02 per cent of global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuel and cement-making.
Much of those emissions come from burning the hydrocarbons the company produces and sells. Shell’s share is more than three times that of Petrobras.

At the heart of the legal argument is an attribution study published in a journal belonging to the Nature group, which estimates that climate change intensified the extreme rainfall in 2024 by 12 per cent.
The plaintiffs want Shell to pay for that additional intensity in proportion to its contribution to global emissions: two per cent of the 12 per cent increase.

“In Brazil, it is the first time that we use attribution science against a carbon major company,” Miola said. “Choosing Shell does not exempt the other companies from being prosecuted in the near future.”
Super typhoon
In the Philippines, too, the plaintiffs want Shell to pay for its history and its size.

In December 2021, Typhoon Rai, known locally as Odette, devastated several islands. More than 400 people died and hundreds of thousands lost their homes. It was one of the worst disasters in the country’s history.
Four years later, in 2025, around 100 survivors, supported by NGOs, filed a lawsuit against Shell in the UK, where the company is based.
The lawyers base their case on the company’s “historic carbon emissions” and the link between those emissions and global warming, which climate scientists have shown intensifies cyclones.
Aggravating factor

The plaintiffs cite an additional aggravating factor: Shell’s “history of misinformation regarding the causes and impacts of climate change,” said Greg Lascelles, a lawyer at Hausfeld, the firm handling the lawsuit in London.
“There’s a lot of evidence about Shell knowing as early as in the 1960s” that fossil fuels contributed to global warming, said Madeleine Lynch, a campaigner on the “Odette case.”
The lawsuit argues that this establishes negligence under Philippine law.
The Brazilian lawsuit also cites Shell’s past record, including an internal company report from 1986 that acknowledged fossil fuels’ role in increasing greenhouse gas emissions and global warming.

Shell has not responded to the Brazilian lawsuit. However, in December, following the Philippine lawsuit, the company said “the suggestion that Shell had unique knowledge about climate change is simply not true.”
‘Test cases’
Claims seeking compensation from major companies for specific climate-related damage — sometimes in countries where those companies are not even based — are only just beginning to emerge.
Swiss cement maker Holcim is being sued by residents of an Indonesian island being eroded by rising sea levels. Pakistani farmers are suing two companies in Germany, including a cement manufacturer.

“The cases we’re seeing in the world are test cases, to see whether it is a viable legal strategy,” said Noah Walker-Crawford, a researcher at the Grantham Research Institute on Climate Change and the Environment at the London School of Economics.
“If these cases are successful,” he said, “We could expect to see a lot more of these cases against more companies as well.” — AFP
197cac23ab866ba2: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the Universiti Malaya (UM) Student Residence project to serve as a model for development management that is clean, efficient, and free from leakages or the wastage of public funds.

He said the implementation of this project must draw lessons from the shortcomings of past project management which led to cost overruns, delays, and abandoned construction sites ultimately resulting in losses for the nation.

“How much national funding has been wasted or lost due to poor management? Therefore, vice-chancellor, ensure that UM and this Student Residence project become an example for other agencies to emulate.

“You can do a great job, a clean job, an incorruptible job, and one carried out with full dedication. This is a real challenge for us,” he said during his inaugural address at the launch of the UM Student Residence project here today.

Also present were Minister of Higher Education Datuk Seri Dr. Zambry Abd Kadir and his deputy, Adam Adli Abd Halim; Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar; and UM vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Seri Dr Noor Azuan Abu Osman.

Anwar said the project in question is a major responsibility that must be carried out with full dedication, requiring the commitment of all involved parties to ensure it is completed according to plan.

He noted that the issue of “leakages” (inefficiencies or losses) does not stem from differences in race, region, or social class; rather, it is linked to dishonest conduct that undermines the national interest.

Consequently, the Prime Minister said he would personally oversee the project’s implementation. He also expressed his desire for it to be completed ahead of the original 2030 schedule, aiming to address the issue of student accommodation specifically the rising cost of house rentals in areas surrounding universities.

To ensure the project is expedited, Anwar said he has directed all government machinery including government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs) to prioritise this initiative.

“This is a priority project for us that must be completed quickly. When you (Azuan) say it will be ready by 2030, I say no. This is a new, efficient Madani government. We will work to ensure it is accelerated,” he said.

The implementation of the UM Student Residence Development Project supports the government’s agenda as announced in the 2027 Budget to address student accommodation needs through infrastructure that is better planned, comfortable, and aligned with current requirements.

Designed to accommodate 40,000 students, the project will be executed in phases: Phase One will cater to 10,000 students, followed by Phase Two, which will provide additional capacity for another 30,000 students.

The residences will offer four categories of accommodation: ‘Standard’ (five rooms for 10 residents), ‘Standard Premium’ (three rooms for six residents), ‘Apartment’ (two rooms for three residents), and ‘Studio’ (for a single resident). All units are planned to be equipped with air-conditioning.

The project is based on a ‘community living’ concept, integrating residential functions with spaces for social interaction and community activities. This aims to foster an environment that encourages character development, social connections, and a sense of togetherness, thereby enriching the students’ overall experience throughout their studies.

Meanwhile, Deputy Minister of Higher Education Adam Adli Abd Halim, speaking to reporters after the event, expressed hope that this initiative would serve as a long-term, sustainable solution to issues concerning student accommodation.
He said the government is committed to ensuring the project proceeds smoothly through a ‘fast-track’ approach, without compromising on integrity or established management procedures.

“This project begins at UM, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), and Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin (UniSZA), with a second phase to follow. I believe we can expand this programme to other universities as well,” he said.

Earlier, in his speech, Azuan said the development of the Student Residences (*Residensi Siswa*) reflects the university’s commitment to prioritising student welfare, alongside its efforts to strengthen academic and research excellence.

“We cannot speak of excellence in higher education without addressing the realities of student life. The need for comfortable, safe, and affordable housing must be a core priority in the university’s development agenda.

“Through the Student Residences, UM aims to ensure that campus development is not focused solely on academic infrastructure, but also delivers tangible benefits to the daily lives of its students,” he said. — Bernama
bbdda3b80d5bc520: X says it has nuked more than 13,000 accounts involved in three suspected foreign influence operations targeting US political debate. In a post on Wednesday evening, the platform linked the operations to Iran, Russia, and China. It said the networks used inauthentic accounts to post and amplify political content targeting candidates and public figures across the political spectrum. The announcement comes ahead of the US midterm elections on November 3. "People come to X to talk about what's happening in the world, including the upcoming 2026 US midterms," the platform said. "Free speech is the bedrock of a functioning democracy, and we are proud that X is the global town square where these debates happen. Our job is to keep that conversation authentic, open, and safe." X did not publicly explain the evidence behind its attribution. Separately, it highlighted its Civic Integrity policy, which covers misleading information about how, when, and where to vote, as well as content intended to discourage participation. Reports submitted under "Civic Integrity" are routed into requests for Community Notes. X says it uses the crowdsourced feature alongside platform moderation and may label policy-breaking posts in critical cases. Community Notes has faced scrutiny. When the European Commission launched formal proceedings against X under the Digital Services Act in 2023, it raised questions about the feature's effectiveness for validating a post's accuracy. X's reliance on crowdsourced context follows layoffs and senior departures from its moderation teams after Musk acquired Twitter. Foreign influence campaigns aren't confined to US elections. MI5 chief Sir Ken McCallum said this week that Russia had attempted to interfere in the 2016 Brexit referendum, but cautioned against treating that as evidence it changed the result. ®
a1fa1e4475e5ba83: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has reverted to the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK) guidelines, which mandate the immediate closure of schools when the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaches 200, following input from various relevant agencies.
Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said that under the PTJK, all outdoor classroom activities must also be halted when the API exceeds 100.
She added that parents are also permitted not to send their children to school if they are concerned that the haze condition could affect their health, provided they notify the school administration.
“In managing the haze, specific actions must be taken for each API reading level. We cannot assume that all risk levels require the same course of action,” she said in a Facebook post today.

She noted that the decision to return to the PTJK guidelines was made after discussions with related agencies, including taking into account views from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) that haze management must be guided by the said plan.

Fadhlina stated that the previous decision to take a more cautious approach was made by taking seriously the concerns expressed by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia regarding the haze situation, while prioritising the safety and health of students.

According to her, the MOE also received various feedback from parents, including requests for schools to be closed for a week, concerns about learning gaps, and the difficulty of managing childcare while working.

Therefore, she said the ministry called upon all relevant agencies such as the Ministry of Health, the Department of Environment (DOE), and the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) for discussions, as the issue involves health, air quality, and disaster management that require their expertise.
“I understand that logic. After all, an API reading of 150 is indeed within the unhealthy category. Parents’ concerns at that level are certainly well-founded,” she said.

Fadhlina stated that the flexibility given for students to be absent from school takes into account differing health conditions among students, including those suffering from asthma, respiratory issues, or those more easily affected by the haze.

She said the MOE is also responsible for ensuring that students do not continuously lose learning time, drawing from the experience during the Movement Control Order (MCO) which highlighted the difficulty of recovering missed learning, while emphasising that every concern will continue to be heard and decisions made in consultation with expert authorities. — Bernama
8f4c4e5a830397e4: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The proposed constitutional amendments to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure and separate the roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor were among the key matters discussed at the 273rd Conference of Rulers meeting at Istana Negara.
The two-day meeting, which began yesterday, was chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the second day’s proceedings, accompanied by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

According to a statement issued by the Office of the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal today, the Conference deliberated on a consultation paper concerning the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026, which proposes limiting the Prime Minister’s tenure.

The Conference was also briefed on the Constitution (Amendment) (No. 2) Bill 2026, concerning the separation of the roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor (AG-PP), as well as proposed amendments to Section 97 of the Child Act 2001.

Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail presented a briefing on national security, while Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman briefed the Conference on defence matters.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir also delivered an economic briefing.

Other matters discussed included the appointment of a Special Court judge, the appointment of the new chairholder for the Institution of Malay Rulers Chair at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), and proposed meeting dates for 2027.

The Conference also discussed matters concerning Islamic religious administration under the National Council for Islamic Religious Affairs Malaysia (MKI), including a proposal to expand the scope of audits of zakat funds.

The meeting was attended by the Malay Rulers and Governors, as well as the Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail, Crown Prince of Kelantan Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra, representing the Sultan of Kelantan, and the Tunku Temenggong of Johor Tunku Idris Iskandar Al-Haj, representing the Regent of Johor. — Bernama
3a9f4367bfa4c83a: Rocket Lab has delayed the maiden launch of its Neutron rocket again, due to carbon composite manufacturing issues. It is more than five years since Rocket Lab said it was developing the launcher, a step up from its workhorse Electron, and capable of sending up to 13,000 kg to Low Earth Orbit. At the time, 2024 was mooted as the first launch date. Then perhaps 2025. Then 2026. And now it is "expected to occur in 2027." It won't be early in 2027 either. During a briefing, boss Peter Beck said he expects to complete testing of the problematic components before the end of Q1 2027, at which point it will set a new launch date. According to Beck, Rocket Lab identified problems with a first-stage tank that failed qualification due to third-party processing. The space biz switched to its own internal processes, and things appeared to be going swimmingly until, Beck said, "we identified an issue with the manufacturing process for the propellant dome." The issue was voids that formed within the carbon composite layers during manufacturing. Beck explained, "They don't necessarily mean that the dome would fail in flight," but they would reduce the margin, so a rethink was required. The good news, according to Beck, is that the problem is solved. The bad news? Dealing with it has delayed things. In August, Rocket Lab said it targeted delivery of Neutron to the launch pad in Q4 2026. Beck now reckons the cryo and hydrostatic test campaigns will not wrap up until Q1 2027. Rocket Lab's shares have taken a battering following the announcement, dropping from about $63 yesterday to near $53 in after-hours trading. When it becomes operational, Neutron will feature an entirely reusable first stage with a "Hungry Hippo" clamshell fairing, opening to deploy a second stage before closing for a return to Earth. The timing of Neutron's availability is of note since it could come as SpaceX reportedly seeks to wind down Falcon 9 in favor of Starship. While Falcon 9 can loft heavier payloads, Neutron's mass capability puts it firmly in the same class. Assuming, of course, it makes it to the launchpad. ®
82f9a25f5bb9a201: KYIV, Oct 15 — Ukraine will no longer abide by US President Donald Trump’s demands not to strike Russian oil refineries, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in remarks published today, amid deepening tensions between the two leaders over a US-Russia diesel agreement.
Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since last week, when Trump eased sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel onto global markets.

Zelensky described the deal as a “weak decision”, saying it would encourage Russia to prolong its four-and-a-half-year war with Ukraine, while several of Ukraine’s European allies criticised the agreement.
Addressing the criticism on Saturday, Trump claimed Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries were to blame for rising diesel prices and said it was “time for Ukraine to get a new president”.
“The block (on attacking refineries) is out,” Zelensky told the Financial Times in an interview published today. “We’re done.”
Trump had announced on Sunday a surprise “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine, which Zelensky said he knew nothing about.
And earlier this week, Ukraine reported disruptions to a critical US satellite communications system that its army uses on the battlefield.
“We need HONESTY from our partners about this war,” Zelensky wrote on social media today.
In an interview with British journalist Piers Morgan yesterday, Zelensky agreed that he felt “betrayed” by Trump’s diesel-supply deal with Russia’s Vladimir Putin.
He also questioned the advice that Trump was receiving, after senior Ukrainian officials in Kyiv openly accused the US of helping Russia.
“It’s painful when President Trump chooses one side, not our side,” he said.
“I think his advisors are wrong... This is not (the) right side of history.”

Since launching a full-scale invasion of its neighbour in 2022, Russia has systematically hit Ukrainian energy infrastructure, leading to energy and heating shortages — while Ukraine has hit back at Russian oil refineries it says fund the war.
More recently, Trump’s war in Iran has led to oil shortages and ensuing price spikes, creating major headwinds for his Republican Party ahead of midterm elections early next month.
Satellite row
The Kremlin accused Ukraine today of derailing US peace efforts by resuming its strikes.
Russia today reported that an oil refinery in Ryazan, south of the capital, Moscow, had been hit in a “large-scale attack”.
Kyiv “continues to launch strikes against these facilities,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters.
“It is coming into serious conflict with the peace efforts of the US and American negotiators, who are making vigorous efforts to initiate the peace process,” he added.

Much of the outrage in Ukraine this week has been over restrictions to the Starshield satellite communications system that its military relies upon to detect incoming Russian attacks and to coordinate its frontline response.
Defence officials confirmed that the US had threatened to withdraw intelligence-sharing if Ukraine continued long-range strikes on Russian oil refineries.
Powerful ballistic missiles struck Kyiv and the surrounding region on Tuesday and yesterday night, before air raid sirens could sound warning people to take cover.
But tech billionaire Elon Musk, who has also called for Zelensky to be replaced as leader, said his SpaceX company was not behind any disruption to the Starshield system.
“Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government,” he said.
“Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” he added, referring to Trump.
Ukraine uses the Starshield system from Musk’s SpaceX for battlefield communications, mid-range strikes on Russian-occupied territory and interceptor drones.
It is separate from the parallel Starlink civilian satellite system, which Ukraine also uses but not for offensive operations.
Speeds were slower yesterday, affecting connectivity, officials said.
Russia has intensified its bombardment of Ukraine and its capital in recent months, leading to mounting civilian casualties and disrupting daily life for citizens.
Moscow currently occupies around a fifth of Ukraine, including Crimea, which it annexed in 2014. — AFP
665b6135e2cb96d0: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.
Pig kidneys that were “frozen” for a year have been brought back to life
Pig kidneys that were cooled to -150 °C and stored in a freezer for months have been successfully rewarmed and shown to work again for the first time, say scientists.

The kidneys, which are similar in size to human ones, were left in a glass-like state, in one case for over a year. Once they had been rewarmed, tested in machines, and transplanted into pigs, the kidneys regained their color and made urine—key signs they were working.
The results are a big milestone. But the team still needs to establish whether the approach could work for humans.
Dissect what the breakthrough means for organ transplantation.
—Jessica Hamzelou
How much more can nuclear power plants give?

In this age of rising electricity demand, people are trying to squeeze every last bit of power out of every power plant. Over the past few weeks, there’s been big news about the nuclear industry trying to do just that.

Constellation, the largest nuclear operator in the US, announced plans to add nearly a gigawatt of new capacity across 11 existing nuclear reactors at six plants. On October 5, the Department of Energy awarded Vistra a $4.2 billion loan to upgrade three plants.
Pushing existing reactors to produce more could quickly provide more clean power for data centers. But just how much additional power can we count on?
Read the full story to find out.

cca602259dec04d3: ISTANBUL, Oct 15 — Istanbul was today battling to recover from flooding caused by what officials said was the heaviest rainfall in the city since records began more than 80 years ago, as the downpour continued.

The rain began lashing Turkey’s largest city in earnest yesterday morning and intensified throughout the day, causing chaos and flash flooding, with footage showing cars being dragged away by the fast-flowing waters.
“We are talking here about the highest level of precipitation in Istanbul since records began in 1942,” Istanbul governor Davut Gul said.

Two people died in the floods, one of them a 14-year-old boy who was electrocuted when he stepped into a puddle in the Balat area. He was rushed to hospital but medical personnel were unable to save him, officials said.
Another three people were being treated in hospital, Gul said.

On yesterday evening, the governor said schools would be shut across Istanbul until Monday, urging people to stay home “unless absolutely necessary” and advising those living in basement properties “to spend the night on safer, higher floors”.
He advised residents to stay away from “stream beds, underpasses and other areas at risk of flooding”.
Dramatic footage posted online and collated by DHA news agency showed a line of parked cars in the northern Sariyer district being pushed into the torrent of muddy water, where they were swept away.

Another showed people being hauled from the raging waters to safety through a first-floor window, while elsewhere two people with umbrellas were seen stepping into the shovel of a large mechanical digger, which took them away.

Forty-three flights bound for Istanbul Airport on the Black Sea had to be diverted, as did three flights heading for the city’s Sabiha Gokcen airport on the Asian side, which also temporarily suspended take-offs due to strong winds, the transport ministry said in a statement carried by state news agency Anadolu.

Turkey’s AFAD disaster agency has set up a crisis desk to manage incidents caused by the heavy rainfall, which by nightfall yesterday had risen to 1,277 flooding incidents, 15 landslides, 47 people stranded and two roofs blown off.
The heavy rains are expected to continue over the weekend. — AFP
98ed15fcaf111b1f: Apple's trade secrets spat with OpenAI has taken a new turn, with the ChatGPT maker accusing a former employee of taking more than 100 confidential files about its unreleased hardware back to Cupertino. In a court filing submitted Wednesday, OpenAI claims the unnamed employee, who joined from Apple before returning to the iPhone maker just six months later, transferred sensitive documents to his personal accounts before leaving. The filing alleges the files included detailed images of at least one unreleased OpenAI device, engineering and manufacturing data, supplier information, and project files, along with specifications for cosmetic finishes and reports on coating and sealing hardware components. According to the filing, some were transferred just after midnight in Singapore on June 2, which the filing claims was the employee's final day at OpenAI. But OpenAI claims the information didn't simply disappear into a personal inbox. According to the filing, the former employee also allegedly presented OpenAI's product plans to Apple's senior leadership, including its vice president of operations in Asia. That presentation apparently happened months ago, and OpenAI is now pointing to Apple's latest push into AI-powered hardware, including its newly announced smart home products, as cause for concern. "OpenAI is very concerned that its trade secret and confidential information is now circulating inside Apple, where Apple engineers can shape Apple's upcoming products based on OpenAI's confidential and innovative work," the company told the court. Apple says it hasn't found anything to back up OpenAI's claims and insists it has rules to stop staff from bringing their former employers' secrets into the company. There's a certain irony here, given that Apple was the one accusing OpenAI of stealing its secrets just a few months ago. Back in July, Apple sued OpenAI and former employees Chang Liu and Tang Yew Tan, alleging they took confidential engineering information to help the ChatGPT maker develop its own hardware. Cupertino alleged that the pair took valuable trade secrets concerning its hardware development, including information about unreleased products, to their new employer. OpenAI denied the accusations, saying at the time: "We have no interest in other companies' trade secrets. We remain focused on building innovative technology that empowers people everywhere." Now the ChatGPT maker is claiming confidential hardware information may have traveled in the opposite direction, though it has yet to establish that Apple received or used any of the allegedly taken material. OpenAI has asked the court for time to investigate the matter and potentially bring counterclaims against Apple. No such counterclaims have yet been filed. For all the talk of groundbreaking AI hardware, the biggest competition right now appears to be over who took whose files. ®

b6c0f2947b7eb01e: ISRAEL-GAZA BORDER, Oct 15 — Israeli opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s main rival in upcoming elections, vowed today to defeat Hamas in Gaza if he becomes prime minister following the October 27 vote.

“Today I give a public commitment: from the moment I enter the Prime Minister’s Office, within 18 months Hamas will no longer rule the Gaza Strip,” the leader of the centre-right Yashar party said at a press conference near the war-ravaged Palestinian territory.

He said he would achieve this either by implementing US President Donald Trump’s ceasefire plan for Gaza, which provides for the gradual disarmament of Hamas and a transfer of power, or through “creative operations” by Israel’s military aimed at destroying the Palestinian movement’s military wing.
The campaign pledge is one of the strongest yet from Eisenkot, a 66-year-old former military chief.
The close-fought election will be the first since Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, which resulted in the deaths of more than 1,200 people.

In response, Israel launched a massive offensive in Gaza that has since killed more than 74,300 people, according to the territory’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas and whose figures are generally considered reliable by the United Nations.
Eisenkot today accused Netanyahu of a “strategic failure” in Gaza, where he said “Hamas is still the sovereign... armed, arming itself, and militarily active” after three years of war.
He also reiterated a pledge to establish a state commission of inquiry to identify those responsible for any security lapses leading up to October 7, a push the government has so far resisted.

Current polls show that neither Netanyahu’s bloc nor that led by Eisenkot are in a position to win the 61 seats needed to control the 120-seat parliament and form a governing coalition. — AFP

66cd3ee9750f0b84: Hackers who broke into the UK's Legal Aid Agency last year stole records dating back nearly five decades, the government has admitted, revealing the breach was far more extensive than previously thought. The Legal Aid Agency said on Wednesday that around 250,000 records stolen in the April 2025 attack date from before 2007, including one going back to 1978. That's much further back than the agency previously estimated ­­– it initially said the stolen data covered legal aid applications, claims, and payments from 2007. Most of the newly identified records date from the 1990s and 2000s, with only a “fractionally small number” originating before 1990. Still, the discovery raises an awkward question about just how much historical personal information was sitting in government systems when the attackers came knocking. That wasn't the only surprise in the stolen data, as the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) has also discovered that hackers accessed information from HM Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS), including names, dates of birth, nationalities, and case reference numbers for offenders supervised by probation services between 2010 and 2017. The government says the probation records concern a relatively small number of offenders, with more than 99 percent of the affected data relating to people under supervision in 2016 and 2017. It stressed that none of the stolen probation information relates to victims of crime. The latest revelations come almost 18 months after the Legal Aid Agency disclosed that criminals had accessed and downloaded a significant amount of sensitive personal information. The agency first detected the intrusion on April 23, 2025, but officials didn't establish the scale of the compromise until May 16. The government subsequently took the LAA's online services offline, leaving lawyers struggling to access the systems they needed to submit claims and manage cases. The disruption dragged on for months, with the agency's troubled return to service in December leaving legal aid providers battling delays and ongoing technical problems. Further forensic work has now revealed that the data theft goes back much further than officials originally believed. The compromised information varies by individual but could include names, addresses, dates of birth, National Insurance numbers, financial details, and information about legal proceedings. Some records also contain details of criminal charges, pleas, convictions, and sentences. Among the older material are records relating to legal aid benefit assessments dating from 1978 to 2012, and payments made under the Very High Cost Cases scheme between 1981 and 2004. The government cautioned that the presence of historical records doesn’t mean that everyone who applied for legal aid before 2007 had their information stolen, nor does the 250,000 figure represent a confirmed number of affected individuals. Explaining why it has taken so long to pin down the extent of the theft, the MoJ said the attackers stole information spread across several complex systems, much of it unstructured, fragmented, or incomplete. "Because of our increased capability to identify data, we have developed a more complete understanding of the information compromised," the agency said. The government says it has no indication that the stolen information has been published or shared, although that offers little certainty to anyone whose personal details may now be in criminal hands. Since the attack, the MoJ says it has tightened authentication and access controls, improved security monitoring, addressed vulnerabilities and begun retiring or isolating higher-risk technology. Work to modernize its legacy systems is also underway. The question of why records stretching back to the 1970s remained accessible in the first place is one the latest update does not answer. ®
be75dc4992b43cee: RIYADH, Oct 15 — The Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis today said it had intercepted a cruise missile in the Medina region — home to one of Islam’s holiest cities, but the Houthis denied carrying out any such attack.
